meta.title: The Spin Catalog — Daily Chapter Readings
meta.purpose: A two-person daily Bible reading wheel. Spin, read the passage, discuss.

display.note: The wheel face should show only topic + reference. hook, question and size are optional metadata for the detail view or filters.

designNotes: Two-stage spin recommended: wheel 1 picks a category, wheel 2 picks an entry within it. Keeps the wheel readable with 250+ entries.
Track used ids in localStorage/DB so a spun entry is not repeated until the catalog is exhausted.
size = rough reading load: short (under ~15 verses), medium (a chapter), long (a chapter or more, or two chapters).
Curated to avoid the most-quoted passages. No Beatitudes, Psalm 23, 1 Corinthians 13, Ephesians 4:1-16, Prodigal Son, Good Samaritan, Armour of God, Psalm 51, Isaiah 53, David and Goliath.

categories.name: Integrity in the Dark
categories.blurb: Who you are when no one is checking.

categories.name: Honest Prayer and Lament
categories.blurb: Prayers that argue, complain, and refuse to be polite.

categories.name: Repentance and Repair
categories.blurb: Confession, restitution, and reconciliation that costs something.

categories.name: Money, Work and Justice
categories.blurb: Wages, land, generosity, and what God says about the poor.

categories.name: Suffering and Endurance
categories.blurb: Faith held under pressure, and prayers that God did not answer yet.

categories.name: Humility and Ambition
categories.blurb: Status, position, pride, and the leaders who fell to it.

categories.name: Calling and Costly Obedience
categories.blurb: Being sent, saying yes, and counting the cost.

categories.name: The Body and Its Fractures
categories.blurb: Life together, disagreement, and how the early church handled it.

categories.name: Wisdom, Time and Mortality

categories.name: Grace, Identity and the Cross

categories.name: The Outsider

categories.name: Strange Chapters

entries.topic: The Covenant of the Arrows
entries.hook: Two friends make a pact that will cost one of them a throne.
entries.question: What is the most expensive thing your friendship has cost either of you?

entries.topic: Kindness Paid to a Dead Man's Son
entries.hook: David keeps a promise years after the man he made it to has died.
entries.question: Who has a claim on your kindness that no one would notice if you dropped?

entries.topic: Seven Days of Saying Nothing
entries.hook: The friends get it right before they open their mouths.
entries.question: When did someone's silence help you more than their advice?

entries.topic: Praying for the Friends Who Wounded You
entries.hook: Job's own restoration begins while he is praying for the men who accused him.
entries.question: Is there someone you owe a prayer rather than a grudge?

entries.topic: Wounds From a Friend, Kisses From an Enemy
entries.hook: Iron sharpening iron, and why flattery is the more dangerous gift.
entries.question: What is one thing you have wanted to say to each other but softened?

entries.topic: The Cord of Three Strands
entries.hook: The cynic of the Old Testament makes his one exception: do not do life alone.
entries.question: Where have you fallen recently with no one there to lift you up?

entries.topic: A Runaway Slave Sent Back as a Brother
entries.hook: The shortest, most awkward letter Paul ever wrote, and he offers to pay the debt himself.
entries.question: Whose debt would you be willing to put on your own account?

entries.topic: When Two Good Men Split Over a Third
entries.hook: Paul and Barnabas separate. Scripture never tells us who was right.
entries.question: Can two people both be right and still have to part ways?

entries.topic: Demas Left. Bring Mark
entries.hook: Paul's last letter is a list of who stayed and who did not.
entries.question: If you wrote this list today, whose name would be on it?

entries.topic: Diotrephes Loves Being First
entries.hook: A one-page letter about a man who would not welcome anyone he did not control.
entries.question: Where do you notice yourself wanting to be first?

entries.topic: The Roll Call Nobody Reads
entries.hook: Twenty-six names, and a woman carrying the letter that changed theology.
entries.question: Who are the unnamed people carrying your work?

entries.topic: Epaphras, Wrestling in Prayer for You
entries.hook: Paul describes a man's prayer life as physical labour on behalf of people far away.
entries.question: Whose name do you carry to God with that kind of effort?

entries.topic: Those Who Stayed With the Baggage
entries.hook: David makes it law: the one who guarded the supplies gets the same share as the one who fought.
entries.question: Who does the unglamorous work in your circle, and do they get credit?

entries.topic: Hands Held Up Until Sundown
entries.hook: The battle turns not on the fighter but on the two men holding his arms.
entries.question: Whose arms are you meant to be holding up this month?

entries.topic: Confronting Peter to His Face
entries.hook: Paul rebukes the chief apostle publicly, over who he was willing to eat with.
entries.question: Do you have permission to correct each other, and do you use it?

entries.topic: Forgive Him Before Grief Swallows Him
entries.hook: Paul warns that punishment held too long is a win for the enemy.
entries.question: Is there discipline in your life that has quietly become punishment?

entries.topic: Barnabas Vouches for the Man Everyone Feared
entries.hook: One man's reputation is spent to get a former persecutor into the room.
entries.question: Whose reputation would you spend yours on?

entries.topic: Going to Tarsus to Find Saul
entries.hook: Barnabas travels to fetch a man who had disappeared for years.
entries.question: Who have you let drift that you should go and find?

entries.topic: Four Friends and a Broken Roof
entries.hook: Jesus responds to their faith, not the paralysed man's.
entries.question: What would you be willing to damage to get a friend in front of God?

entries.topic: Would That All the Lord's People Prophesied
entries.hook: Joshua wants two unauthorised men stopped. Moses refuses to be threatened.
entries.question: Do you celebrate or resent gifting outside your own group?

entries.topic: The Three Who Broke Through for a Cup of Water
entries.hook: David refuses to drink it. He pours it out as an offering instead.
entries.question: What loyalty have you received that you did not know how to honour?

entries.topic: By Many or By Few
entries.hook: Jonathan and his armour-bearer attack a garrison alone, on a maybe.
entries.question: Is there something you are waiting for permission to attempt?

entries.topic: How Good and Pleasant
entries.hook: Three verses on unity, using the image of oil running down a beard.
entries.question: What actually breaks unity between you two, in practice?

entries.topic: The Governor Who Refused His Own Salary
entries.hook: He cancels debts, confronts the lenders, and declines the food allowance he was entitled to.
entries.question: What are you entitled to that it might be better not to take?

entries.topic: I Am Doing a Great Work; I Cannot Come Down
entries.hook: Four invitations, one smear campaign, and one hired prophet, all aimed at getting him off the wall.
entries.question: What is the distraction that keeps successfully pulling you down?

entries.topic: The Servant Who Ran After the Money
entries.hook: Gehazi takes what his master refused, and lies about where he has been.
entries.question: What small private taking have you told yourself is fine?

entries.topic: Striking the Rock
entries.hook: One act of temper in forty years, and Moses does not enter the land.
entries.question: Is that fair? Sit with the discomfort before answering.

entries.topic: The Cave and the Cut Robe
entries.hook: The opportunity is perfect, the justification is easy, and David's conscience strikes him anyway.
entries.question: When did you last feel guilty about something technically allowed?

entries.topic: The Spear and the Water Jar
entries.hook: The second time is harder. Everyone around him says God has arranged it.
entries.question: How do you tell God's provision from a convenient opportunity?

entries.topic: I Will Not Offer What Costs Me Nothing
entries.hook: The land is offered free. David insists on paying full price.
entries.question: Where is your giving currently costing you nothing?

entries.topic: Seven Things the Lord Hates
entries.hook: Four of the seven are about what we do with our mouths.
entries.question: Which of the seven is nearest to your own habits?

entries.topic: A Covenant With My Eyes
entries.hook: Job's sworn oath of innocence, item by item, including how he treated his servants.
entries.question: Could you take this oath clause by clause? Where would you stop?

entries.topic: Who May Dwell on Your Holy Hill?
entries.hook: The answer includes keeping a promise even after it turns out to hurt you.
entries.question: What promise are you currently regretting, and will you keep it?

entries.topic: The Charter for a Household
entries.hook: A king writes rules for his private life, including what he will not look at.
entries.question: Write your own version of verse 3. What goes on your list?

entries.topic: Do You Seek Great Things for Yourself?
entries.hook: Five verses to a burnt-out secretary, telling him to lower his ambitions and live.
entries.question: What great thing are you seeking that God may not be offering?

entries.topic: Panelled Houses, Ruined Temple
entries.hook: They finished their own homes first, then wondered why nothing satisfied.
entries.question: What have you finished for yourself while something else stayed unbuilt?

entries.topic: Was It for Me That You Fasted?
entries.hook: Seventy years of religious fasting, and God asks who it was actually for.
entries.question: Which of your spiritual habits is really about you?

entries.topic: Priests Who Made Many Stumble
entries.hook: The charge is not immorality. It is teaching in a way that showed partiality.
entries.question: Who might be stumbling over something you said casually?

entries.topic: The Book of Remembrance
entries.hook: God overhears people complaining that serving him is pointless, and has their conversations written down.
entries.question: Have you ever said serving God was not worth it? Was that heard?

entries.topic: The Family That Would Not Drink
entries.hook: God uses one clan's obedience to a dead ancestor to shame a nation.
entries.question: What did your family teach you that you have kept without being watched?

entries.topic: Nadab, Abihu, and Aaron's Silence
entries.hook: Two priests improvise. Their father is not allowed to mourn them.
entries.question: What does this text do to your idea of God? Say it honestly.

entries.topic: The Man of God Who Believed the Wrong Prophet
entries.hook: He resists a king successfully, then is undone by an old man claiming a newer word from God.
entries.question: How do you test a message that contradicts what you already know?

entries.topic: Godliness With Contentment
entries.hook: The love of money as a root, and the instruction to the already rich.
entries.question: What amount would be enough? Say the number out loud.

entries.topic: Achan's Tent
entries.hook: One man's hidden loot, and an entire army loses a battle it should have won.
entries.question: Does private sin really have public cost? Give an example.

entries.topic: Do Not Move the Ancient Landmark
entries.hook: Quiet theft from the powerless, and then a startlingly vivid picture of drunkenness.
entries.question: Which warning here do you least want to hear?

entries.topic: Until I Entered the Sanctuary
entries.hook: A worship leader admits he almost lost his faith envying corrupt people who were doing fine.
entries.question: Whose prosperity has made you doubt that following God pays?

entries.topic: Darkness Is My Closest Companion
entries.hook: The only psalm that never resolves. It ends in the dark.
entries.question: Why do you think God let a prayer like this into the Bible?

entries.topic: Awake! Why Are You Sleeping?
entries.hook: A nation insists it has been faithful and demands to know why it lost anyway.
entries.question: Have you ever been angry at God and called it something else?

entries.topic: Teach Us to Number Our Days
entries.hook: Moses does the arithmetic of a human lifespan and asks for wisdom, not more time.
entries.question: If you knew your number, what would you change tomorrow?

entries.topic: How Long, O Lord?
entries.hook: The prophet complains about injustice. God's answer makes it worse.
entries.question: What answer from God would you struggle to accept?

entries.topic: Though the Fig Tree Does Not Blossom
entries.hook: He decides to rejoice before anything has improved.
entries.question: Can you say verse 17 with specifics from your own life?

entries.topic: You Deceived Me and I Was Deceived
entries.hook: A prophet accuses God of tricking him, then curses the day he was born.
entries.question: What is the most honest thing you have never said to God?

entries.topic: New Every Morning, Said From the Ash Heap
entries.hook: The famous verse sits inside sixty-six verses of siege, hunger and rage.
entries.question: Does knowing the context change how you use that verse?

entries.topic: We Have Sinned, Not They
entries.hook: The one righteous man in the book confesses in the first person plural.
entries.question: What corporate sin could you honestly own as ours?

entries.topic: The Long Prayer That Retells Everything
entries.hook: A whole national history prayed back to God, failures included.
entries.question: Tell each other your own history with God in five minutes.

entries.topic: Too Ashamed to Lift My Face
entries.hook: Ezra tears his clothes and sits appalled until the evening sacrifice.
entries.question: When did you last feel shame on behalf of your community?

entries.topic: And Also the Foreigner Who Comes
entries.hook: At the temple's peak moment, Solomon prays for people who do not belong to Israel.
entries.question: Who is outside your prayers who should be inside them?

entries.topic: We Do Not Know What to Do
entries.hook: A king admits total helplessness in public, then sends the choir out ahead of the army.
entries.question: What are you pretending to have a plan for?

entries.topic: Bargaining Down to Ten
entries.hook: Abraham negotiates with God and God lets him.
entries.question: Why do you think Abraham stopped at ten?

entries.topic: Blot Me Out of Your Book
entries.hook: Moses offers his own salvation in exchange for the people who just betrayed him.
entries.question: Who would you pray that for?

entries.topic: The Neighbour Who Knocks at Midnight
entries.hook: The point is not persistence. It is shamelessness.
entries.question: What have you stopped asking for because you felt embarrassed?

entries.topic: The Widow Who Wore the Judge Down
entries.hook: Jesus ends the parable with a question about whether he will find faith at all.
entries.question: What request have you quietly given up on?

entries.topic: What Paul Actually Asks God For
entries.hook: Not health, not money, not open doors. Endurance with joy.
entries.question: Compare your prayer list to Paul's. What is missing?

entries.topic: A Weaned Child With Its Mother
entries.hook: Three verses about deliberately not occupying yourself with things too great for you.
entries.question: What question are you carrying that is not yours to answer?

entries.topic: Prayer From Inside the Fish
entries.hook: A prayer of thanksgiving offered before anything has changed.
entries.question: Can you thank God from inside the situation, not after it?

entries.topic: Your Words Were Heard From the First Day
entries.hook: The answer left immediately. It arrived twenty-one days later.
entries.question: How do you interpret God's silence? What are the options?

entries.topic: Let Me Know How Fleeting I Am
entries.hook: He tries to stay silent out of reverence, and the silence makes it worse.
entries.question: What are you not saying to God out of fear it is disrespectful?

entries.topic: Search Me and Know My Anxious Thoughts
entries.hook: The uncomfortable end of a well-loved psalm: hatred, then a request to be examined.
entries.question: Are you willing to pray verses 23 and 24 and mean it?

entries.topic: While I Kept Silent My Bones Wasted Away
entries.hook: Unconfessed sin described as a physical illness.
entries.question: What is costing you energy just to keep hidden?

entries.topic: You Are the Man
entries.hook: Nathan makes David sentence himself before revealing the defendant.
entries.question: Why is it easier to see the sin when it is someone else's story?

entries.topic: Take With You Words and Return
entries.hook: God writes the confession for them because they do not know what to say.
entries.question: What would you say if you had the words?

entries.topic: The Years the Locust Has Eaten
entries.hook: Rend your hearts, not your garments. Then a promise about lost time.
entries.question: What years feel eaten? Can they be restored?

entries.topic: You Meant Evil, God Meant Good
entries.hook: The brothers invent a message from their dead father because they still do not trust him.
entries.question: Is there forgiveness you have received but never really believed?

entries.topic: Weeping Loud Enough for Pharaoh to Hear
entries.hook: Joseph clears the room before he breaks.
entries.question: Where do you take your grief, and who is allowed to see it?

entries.topic: Go and Tell Him His Fault, Alone
entries.hook: A four-step process, immediately followed by a parable about a man who skipped the mercy.
entries.question: Which step do you usually skip? Usually the first.

entries.topic: Half My Goods, and Four Times Back
entries.hook: Repentance with a spreadsheet attached.
entries.question: What would repentance cost you in actual money?

entries.topic: Godly Grief and Worldly Grief
entries.hook: One kind of sorrow produces change. The other produces death.
entries.question: Which kind was your last regret?

entries.topic: If We Say We Have No Sin
entries.hook: Walking in the light is not sinlessness. It is refusing to hide.
entries.question: What are you currently in the dark about with each other?

entries.topic: Restitution Plus a Fifth
entries.hook: You return what you took, then add twenty percent, then bring the offering.
entries.question: Is there something you should return before you next pray?

entries.topic: Confess to One Another and Pray
entries.hook: Confession is prescribed horizontally, not just vertically.
entries.question: What makes confessing to a person harder than confessing to God?

entries.topic: Seven Times a Day
entries.hook: The disciples respond to this command by begging for more faith.
entries.question: Who are you on your last forgiveness with?

entries.topic: Forgiveness, That You May Be Feared
entries.hook: A strange logic: mercy is what produces reverence, not punishment.
entries.question: Has being forgiven ever made you take God more seriously?

entries.topic: The Worst King in Judah Prays From Prison
entries.hook: Manasseh sacrificed his own children. He is forgiven and restored.
entries.question: Is there anyone you think is beyond this?

entries.topic: The Book Found in the Rubble
entries.hook: A king hears Scripture for the first time and tears his clothes.
entries.question: When did Scripture last actually disturb you?

entries.topic: Return, Faithless Israel
entries.hook: God speaks to a nation as a husband whose wife left, and still says come back.
entries.question: What does it do to you that God pleads?

entries.topic: The Rudder, the Spark, the Spring
entries.hook: Three images for something no human being has ever tamed.
entries.question: What did you say this week that you would take back?

entries.topic: Firebrands, Arrows, and Death
entries.hook: The man who deceives and then says he was only joking.
entries.question: Have you used humour to say something you actually meant?

entries.topic: Apples of Gold, and Feet That Visit Too Often
entries.hook: Timing, restraint, and knowing when to leave someone's house.
entries.question: Which relationship needs more space, not more effort?

entries.topic: The First to State His Case Seems Right
entries.hook: Then the other party arrives and examines him.
entries.question: When did you last change your mind after hearing the second side?

entries.topic: Every Careless Word
entries.hook: The account will include the throwaway lines, not just the speeches.
entries.question: What does your speech reveal about the tree it comes from?

entries.topic: Let Your Words Be Few
entries.hook: Guard your steps when you go to God's house. Better not to vow than to vow and not pay.
entries.question: What have you promised God and not delivered?

entries.topic: Take Off, Put On
entries.hook: A wardrobe metaphor for character, with a list of what goes in the bin.
entries.question: Pick one item from each list. Name it out loud.

entries.topic: Where Do Quarrels Come From?
entries.hook: The answer is not the other person.
entries.question: What desire is under your most recent argument?

entries.topic: Quick to Hear, Slow to Speak
entries.hook: The man who looks in the mirror and immediately forgets his own face.
entries.question: What conviction did you have last month that you have already forgotten?

entries.topic: You Who Judge Practise the Same Things
entries.hook: Paul says the judgment you pass is a confession.
entries.question: What do you criticise most in others? Look there first.

entries.topic: The Altar That Nearly Started a Civil War
entries.hook: An army mobilises over a misunderstanding. Someone finally sends a delegation to ask.
entries.question: What assumption about someone have you never actually checked?

entries.topic: A Soft Answer, and the Cheerful Look
entries.hook: Thirty-three verses on tone, most of them about what the face does.
entries.question: What does your face say before your mouth opens?

entries.topic: Poverty Overflowing in Generosity
entries.hook: Churches in severe affliction begged for the privilege of giving.
entries.question: Have you ever begged to be allowed to give? Why not?

entries.topic: Open Your Hand Wide: The Year of Release
entries.hook: God anticipates the calculation people will make as the seventh year approaches, and forbids it.
entries.question: Have you ever declined to help because of the timing?

entries.topic: Leave the Corners of Your Field
entries.hook: Justice legislated into farming practice, wages, courts and speech.
entries.question: What are the corners of your income that you should stop harvesting?

entries.topic: The Year Everything Goes Back
entries.hook: Every fifty years, land returns and debts die. Wealth cannot compound forever.
entries.question: What would a personal jubilee look like for you?

entries.topic: Do Not Sleep on a Poor Man's Cloak
entries.hook: Pay the day labourer before sunset. He is counting on it.
entries.question: Who is waiting on money from you right now?

entries.topic: The Wages You Held Back Are Shouting
entries.hook: Withheld pay has a voice and God is listening to it.
entries.question: Where does your money come from, and who was paid along the way?

entries.topic: Making the Measure Small
entries.hook: They cannot wait for the Sabbath to end so they can go back to cheating.
entries.question: Where do you shave a little off the measure?

entries.topic: The Fast That God Chooses
entries.hook: God rejects their fasting and describes the one he wanted instead.
entries.question: What if your next fast was from something other than food?

entries.topic: The Dishonest Manager Jesus Commended
entries.hook: The most confusing parable Jesus told. He praises a man for fraud.
entries.question: What do you think he is actually commending?

entries.topic: The Man Who Built Bigger Barns
entries.hook: The rich fool's only sin was a very sensible savings plan.
entries.question: At what point does prudence become the sin described here?

entries.topic: Invite the Ones Who Cannot Repay
entries.hook: Jesus watches guests choosing seats and turns it into a rule for guest lists.
entries.question: Who is on your invitation list because of what they can do for you?

entries.topic: Everything in Common, and Two Who Lied
entries.hook: The sin was not keeping the money. It was pretending they had not.
entries.question: Where does your generosity have an audience in mind?

entries.topic: Widows, Real Widows, and Your Own Household
entries.hook: Paul builds a means test, and calls neglecting your relatives worse than unbelief.
entries.question: Which relative is your responsibility and not the church's?

entries.topic: Do Not Withhold Good When You Can Give It
entries.hook: Do not tell your neighbour to come back tomorrow when you have it today.
entries.question: What have you delayed that you could do this week?

entries.topic: Lest You Say My Power Made This Wealth
entries.hook: The danger is not the desert. It is the good land afterwards.
entries.question: What do you credit yourself for that was given to you?

entries.topic: Naboth's Vineyard
entries.hook: A king sulks, a queen arranges a legal murder, and a family loses its inheritance.
entries.question: Where have you seen procedure used to do something wicked?

entries.topic: Give Me Neither Poverty Nor Riches
entries.hook: Agur asks God to keep him from both extremes, and explains the specific danger of each.
entries.question: Which extreme is more dangerous for you personally?

entries.topic: I Was Hungry
entries.hook: Neither group recognised who they were dealing with.
entries.question: Who did you walk past this week?

entries.topic: The Field of the Sluggard
entries.hook: A wall does not collapse suddenly. It collapses by a little sleep at a time.
entries.question: Which wall in your life is quietly falling down?

entries.topic: Aspire to Live Quietly
entries.hook: An ambition Paul commands: mind your business and work with your hands.
entries.question: Whose business are you in that is not yours?

entries.topic: Idle Busybodies
entries.hook: Paul links not working to interfering, and treats it as a discipline issue.
entries.question: Is there work you are avoiding by staying busy elsewhere?

entries.topic: Two Handfuls Rather Than Both Fists Full
entries.hook: A man with no son and no brother, still working himself to death. For whom?
entries.question: Who are you working this hard for?

entries.topic: Treasure in Clay Pots
entries.hook: Pressed but not crushed. The container is deliberately cheap.
entries.question: What is currently pressing you, and what has it not done to you?

entries.topic: The Resume of Weakness
entries.hook: Forced to boast, Paul lists beatings, shipwrecks, and being lowered out of a window in a basket.
entries.question: What would your list contain if you boasted the way Paul does?

entries.topic: The Thorn That Stayed
entries.hook: Three requests, one refusal, and a reason.
entries.question: What have you asked God for three times?

entries.topic: Those Who Did Not Receive the Promise
entries.hook: The faith chapter ends with sawing, stoning, and people who died with nothing.
entries.question: Is faith still faith if it does not work out?

entries.topic: The Root of Bitterness
entries.hook: Discipline as evidence of sonship, and a bitterness that defiles many, not just you.
entries.question: What bitterness of yours has affected other people?

entries.topic: Do Not Be Surprised at the Fire
entries.hook: Suffering as a Christian is normal. Suffering as a meddler is not.
entries.question: Is your current difficulty from faithfulness or from foolishness?

entries.topic: Suffering Produces Endurance
entries.hook: A chain: suffering, endurance, character, hope. No shortcuts in it.
entries.question: Which link in that chain are you on?

entries.topic: Where Were You?
entries.hook: God's answer to the problem of suffering is a tour of the weather.
entries.question: Why does this satisfy Job? Would it satisfy you?

entries.topic: If I Go Forward He Is Not There
entries.hook: He searches in every direction and finds nothing, and still says he will come out as gold.
entries.question: Can you trust a God you cannot currently locate?

entries.topic: Buying a Field in a Doomed City
entries.hook: The Babylonians are at the wall and God tells him to sign a property deed.
entries.question: What long-term thing should you commit to despite the outlook?

entries.topic: Onesiphorus Was Not Ashamed of My Chains
entries.hook: One man searched Rome hard until he found the prisoner nobody else wanted to visit.
entries.question: Who is in a situation embarrassing enough that people have stopped calling?

entries.topic: Midnight Singing in the Stocks
entries.hook: Beaten, bleeding, singing, and then refusing to leave quietly.
entries.question: What are you owed that you should insist on, and what should you let go?

entries.topic: But If Not
entries.hook: Three men state that God can rescue them, and that they will refuse regardless.
entries.question: Is your obedience conditional on the outcome?

entries.topic: Poor, Slandered, and Rich
entries.hook: The one church Jesus has no complaint about is the one being crushed.
entries.question: What would Jesus write to your church in four verses?

entries.topic: Little Power, Open Door
entries.hook: He commends them for small strength, kept word, and an unashamed name.
entries.question: Where are you waiting for more capacity before you obey?

entries.topic: Has God Forgotten to Be Gracious?
entries.hook: He stops asking questions and starts rehearsing history instead.
entries.question: What has God done before that you need to say out loud again?

entries.topic: Wrestling Until Daybreak
entries.hook: He gets the blessing and the limp in the same encounter.
entries.question: What has God given you that came with permanent damage?

entries.topic: The Woman Who Guarded the Bodies
entries.hook: Rizpah sits on a rock for months keeping birds off her sons, until the king notices.
entries.question: What grief have you seen that nobody responded to?

entries.topic: The Broom Tree and the Whisper
entries.hook: God's first response to a suicidal prophet is food and sleep.
entries.question: What is your first move when someone is at the end? Compare it to God's.

entries.topic: Leadership in a Shipwreck
entries.hook: A prisoner ends up running the ship, mostly by making everyone eat.
entries.question: What practical thing helps most in a crisis?

entries.topic: A Bruised Reed He Will Not Break
entries.hook: The servant does not shout, and does not finish off what is already nearly broken.
entries.question: Who around you is a smouldering wick right now?

entries.topic: The Basin and the Towel
entries.hook: He washes the feet of the man he knows is about to sell him.
entries.question: Could you serve someone while knowing what they were planning?

entries.topic: Arguing About Greatness on the Road
entries.hook: He asks what they were discussing. They go quiet.
entries.question: What conversation of yours would go quiet if Jesus asked?

entries.topic: Can We Sit at Your Right and Left?
entries.hook: They ask for position immediately after he predicts his own death.
entries.question: What do you want from God that is really about status?

entries.topic: Timothy and Epaphroditus
entries.hook: Paul says everyone else looks after their own interests. These two did not.
entries.question: Would Paul be able to say that about you?

entries.topic: A Dispute at the Last Supper
entries.hook: The argument about rank happens at the table, hours before the arrest.
entries.question: What is the worst timing you have had for a petty argument?

entries.topic: Clothe Yourselves With Humility
entries.hook: Shepherd willingly, not for money, not domineering. Then cast your anxiety.
entries.question: Where does your leadership tip into control?

entries.topic: Miriam Speaks Against Moses
entries.hook: The complaint is about his wife. The real issue is whose voice counts.
entries.question: What criticism have you made where the stated reason was not the real one?

entries.topic: The King Who Listened to the Wrong Advisers
entries.hook: Rehoboam consults the elders, dislikes the answer, and asks his friends instead.
entries.question: Whose advice do you seek when you already know what you want to hear?

entries.topic: The Trees Who Wanted a King
entries.hook: The olive, fig and vine all decline. Only the thorn bush volunteers.
entries.question: Why is it often the least suitable person who wants the job?

entries.topic: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice
entries.hook: Saul obeys ninety percent, keeps the best animals for worship, and loses the kingdom.
entries.question: Where is your obedience ninety percent?

entries.topic: Showing the Treasury to the Envoys
entries.hook: A good king shows off everything to foreign visitors and dooms his descendants.
entries.question: What do you show people that you should keep quiet about?

entries.topic: The King Who Burned Incense Anyway
entries.hook: He was strong until he was strong, and then his strength destroyed him.
entries.question: What are you good at that has started to make you unaccountable?

entries.topic: For the Man the King Delights to Honour
entries.hook: Haman designs his enemy's honour parade by assuming it is for himself.
entries.question: Where do you assume the compliment is about you?

entries.topic: Grass Eaten in the Field
entries.hook: The most powerful man alive writes his own testimony of losing his mind.
entries.question: What would it take to humble you? Be specific.

entries.topic: The Alliance That Cost Him His Feet
entries.hook: Asa solves a problem cleverly, jails the prophet who says so, and then will not consult God even when ill.
entries.question: What problem have you solved in a way you would rather not examine?

entries.topic: Korah's Rebellion
entries.hook: The rebels' argument sounds spiritual: all the congregation is holy.
entries.question: How do you tell a prophetic challenge from a power grab?

entries.topic: Rights I Refuse to Use
entries.hook: Paul builds a legal case for being paid, then says he will never claim it.
entries.question: What right could you give up for the sake of someone else's faith?

entries.topic: The Older Brother in the Field
entries.hook: The son who never left is the one standing outside at the end.
entries.question: Where does your faithfulness make you resentful?

entries.topic: Count the Cost Before the Foundation
entries.hook: Jesus actively tries to reduce the size of the crowd following him.
entries.question: What has following Christ actually cost you so far?

entries.topic: Let Me First Go Bury My Father
entries.hook: Three volunteers, three answers, none of them encouraging.
entries.question: What is your reasonable-sounding first?

entries.topic: Take Up the Cross
entries.hook: Said to a crowd, not to the twelve.
entries.question: What does denying yourself look like on an ordinary Tuesday?

entries.topic: The Farewell at Miletus
entries.hook: He tells them chains await him and that they will never see his face again.
entries.question: What would you say to your people if you knew it was the last time?

entries.topic: Sheep Among Wolves
entries.hook: The mission briefing includes betrayal by relatives and a sword instead of peace.
entries.question: Has your faith ever divided your family?

entries.topic: Soldier, Athlete, Farmer
entries.hook: Three pictures of long obedience, all of them about not getting distracted.
entries.question: Which image describes your current season?

entries.topic: I Am Only a Youth
entries.hook: God rejects his excuse and then warns him not to be dismayed by their faces.
entries.question: Whose face are you afraid of?

entries.topic: Eat the Scroll; Be a Watchman
entries.hook: Sweet in the mouth, then seven days sitting stunned among the exiles.
entries.question: What truth have you swallowed that you have not digested?

entries.topic: Angry Enough to Die Over a Plant
entries.hook: The book ends with a question and no answer from Jonah.
entries.question: Whose repentance would irritate you?

entries.topic: A Chariot, a Scroll, and a Question
entries.hook: Philip leaves a revival to go stand on a desert road.
entries.question: What smaller assignment might God be giving you?

entries.topic: The Altar to an Unknown God
entries.hook: Paul quotes their poets, not their scriptures. Some sneer, some believe.
entries.question: What is the equivalent altar in the world you move in?

entries.topic: I Was No Prophet, I Was a Herdsman
entries.hook: Told to go earn his bread somewhere else, he explains he did not apply for this.
entries.question: What are you doing that you never chose?

entries.topic: Excuse After Excuse at the Bush
entries.hook: God answers four objections and gets angry at the fifth.
entries.question: What is your fifth excuse?

entries.topic: Give Me This Hill Country
entries.hook: At eighty-five, Caleb asks for the part with giants and fortified cities in it.
entries.question: What would you ask for if age were not an argument?

entries.topic: Straining Forward
entries.hook: Paul lists an impressive CV and calls it rubbish.
entries.question: What on your CV would be hardest to call rubbish?

entries.topic: You Will Wear Yourself Out
entries.hook: A foreign father-in-law reorganises Israel's judiciary over a single conversation.
entries.question: What are you doing alone that should be delegated?

entries.topic: The Report of the Ten
entries.hook: Everyone saw the same land. The difference was who they compared the giants to.
entries.question: What are you measuring your obstacle against?

entries.topic: Reduced to Three Hundred
entries.hook: God keeps shrinking the army so the win cannot be claimed.
entries.question: What resource might God be removing on purpose?

entries.topic: Whom Shall I Send?
entries.hook: The commission he accepts is to preach to people who will not listen.
entries.question: Would you say yes to a calling that was promised to fail?

entries.topic: Marry the Unfaithful Woman Again
entries.hook: God asks a prophet to buy his own wife back from the man she left him for.
entries.question: What does this cost God, if it is a picture of him?

entries.topic: The Wife of Your Youth
entries.hook: God says he will not accept their worship because of how they treat their wives.
entries.question: Can worship be invalidated by home life? What does that mean practically?

entries.topic: Remain As You Are
entries.hook: Paul treats singleness as an advantage rather than a waiting room.
entries.question: What are you postponing until your status changes?

entries.topic: A Servant's Prayer at a Well
entries.hook: An unnamed servant sets a test, and the answer arrives before he finishes praying.
entries.question: How do you decide whether something is guidance or coincidence?

entries.topic: It Is Well
entries.hook: Her son is dead in the room upstairs and she says it is well.
entries.question: What do you say to people while you are still deciding what you believe?

entries.topic: Drink Water From Your Own Cistern
entries.hook: A father describes the end of the road before describing the pleasure at the start.
entries.question: What safeguards do you actually have, not just intend to have?

entries.topic: Set Me as a Seal
entries.hook: Love as strong as death, and unbuyable at any price.
entries.question: What has someone tried to buy from you that was not for sale?

entries.topic: So That Your Prayers Are Not Hindered
entries.hook: Peter says a man's treatment of his wife can block his prayer line.
entries.question: Is there a relationship currently interfering with your prayer life?

entries.topic: On the Doorposts, on the Road, at Bedtime
entries.hook: Faith transmitted through ordinary repetition rather than special events.
entries.question: What are you repeating often enough for someone to inherit it?

entries.topic: Tell the Next Generation
entries.hook: The instruction includes telling them about the failures, not only the victories.
entries.question: What failure of yours should be told rather than hidden?

entries.topic: The Faith of Lois and Eunice
entries.hook: Paul traces Timothy's faith back through his mother to his grandmother.
entries.question: Who is two generations behind your faith?

entries.topic: Meeting the Brother You Cheated
entries.hook: Jacob arranges his family in order of who he is willing to lose first.
entries.question: What does that arrangement reveal about him? About you?

entries.topic: You Choose First
entries.hook: The older man surrenders his right of first choice to end a family quarrel.
entries.question: What would you give up to keep peace in your family?

entries.topic: Hannah's Vow and Eli's Mistake
entries.hook: The priest assumes the praying woman is drunk.
entries.question: Who have you misread because their pain looked like something else?

entries.topic: The Sons Eli Would Not Restrain
entries.hook: He rebukes them mildly and God calls that honouring them above himself.
entries.question: Where is your gentleness actually avoidance?

entries.topic: Widow's Oil, Two Jars at a Time
entries.hook: The oil stops flowing exactly when the borrowed containers run out.
entries.question: Have you limited what God can give by what you were willing to ask for?

entries.topic: The Threshing Floor at Midnight
entries.hook: A foreign widow makes a legal claim in a risky, unconventional way.
entries.question: What legitimate thing do you need to ask for directly?

entries.topic: Children Are a Heritage, and a Quiver
entries.hook: Anxious early rising and late nights called pointless before it turns to children.
entries.question: What are you building that God is not in?

entries.topic: Eating While Your Brother Goes Hungry
entries.hook: Paul says their communion does more harm than good because of who eats first.
entries.question: Where does your church quietly reproduce social divisions?

entries.topic: Building Up, Not Showing Off
entries.hook: The test for every gift in the room is whether an outsider understood anything.
entries.question: Would a visitor to your gathering understand what is happening?

entries.topic: The Weak Brother and the Disputed Menu
entries.hook: Paul refuses to settle who is right and settles who must yield instead.
entries.question: What is your version of the meat question?

entries.topic: Bear With the Failings of the Weak
entries.hook: The strong exist to carry, not to be admired.
entries.question: Who do you find it hardest to be patient with, and why?

entries.topic: The Widows Who Were Overlooked
entries.hook: An ethnic complaint about food distribution, solved by handing power to the complaining group.
entries.question: Which group in your church is being missed right now?

entries.topic: The Council That Wrote a Letter
entries.hook: Sharp debate, testimony, Scripture, then a decision that costs the majority something.
entries.question: How do you two handle a disagreement you cannot resolve quickly?

entries.topic: Lawsuits Between Brothers
entries.hook: Paul says losing is better than winning in public.
entries.question: When was accepting a loss the more Christian option?

entries.topic: Provoke One Another to Love
entries.hook: The word is closer to irritate than encourage. Meeting together is the mechanism.
entries.question: Who provokes you towards good, and how?

entries.topic: Hospitality, Prisoners, and Leaders
entries.hook: Remember prisoners as though you were in prison with them.
entries.question: Whose suffering could you imagine into more honestly?

entries.topic: You Have Abandoned Your First Love
entries.hook: Doctrinally sound, hardworking, patient, and about to have their lampstand removed.
entries.question: What can you do correctly without love and still be commended for?

entries.topic: Lukewarm, Rich, and Naked
entries.hook: Their self-assessment and Christ's assessment do not match at any point.
entries.question: Where might your self-assessment be furthest off?

entries.topic: A Rapid List for Life Together
entries.hook: Around twenty commands in fifteen verses, including help the weak and test everything.
entries.question: Pick the one you are worst at. Start there this week.

entries.topic: Hidden Reefs at Your Love Feasts
entries.hook: Waterless clouds, fruitless trees, wandering stars, all sitting at the shared meal.
entries.question: How do you name a problem person without becoming one?

entries.topic: The Kind of People Who Should Lead
entries.hook: Almost every requirement is about character and household, not ability.
entries.question: Which single item on this list disqualifies most people you know?

entries.topic: Trowel in One Hand, Sword in the Other
entries.hook: Families are stationed to defend their own section of wall.
entries.question: What is your section, and are you guarding it?

entries.topic: They Wept When They Understood
entries.hook: Six hours of public reading, translators explaining as they go, and then an order to stop crying and eat.
entries.question: When did Scripture last move you to tears or laughter?

entries.topic: That They May Be One
entries.hook: Hours from arrest, what he prays about is our unity.
entries.question: If this was his priority, how is it ours?

entries.topic: The Dividing Wall Pulled Down
entries.hook: Peace is described as a demolished barrier, not a good feeling.
entries.question: What wall exists in your church that Christ has already demolished?

entries.topic: Restore Him Gently; Carry Your Own Load
entries.hook: Two commands that look contradictory: bear each other's burdens, and each carry his own load.
entries.question: Which one do you need to hear more today?

entries.topic: Today, While It Is Called Today
entries.hook: Daily encouragement prescribed as protection against a slowly hardening heart.
entries.question: What has hardened in you over the last year?

entries.topic: No Partiality for the Gold Ring
entries.hook: Seating arrangements as a theological failure.
entries.question: Who gets your best attention, and why?

entries.topic: Like a Nursing Mother, Like a Father
entries.hook: Paul describes ministry with no flattery, no greed, and no pretext.
entries.question: Is there flattery in how you lead or serve?

entries.topic: Better the House of Mourning
entries.hook: A funeral teaches you more than a party, and do not ask why the old days were better.
entries.question: What did a funeral teach you that nothing else could?

entries.topic: Whatever Your Hand Finds to Do
entries.hook: The same fate for everyone, and a forgotten poor man who once saved a city.
entries.question: Would you still do the good thing if no one ever remembered?

entries.topic: Before the Silver Cord Snaps
entries.hook: Old age described as a house whose keepers tremble and whose windows go dim.
entries.question: What are you doing now that your older self will thank you for?

entries.topic: A Season, and the Question Underneath
entries.hook: Read past verse eight to the part about eternity in the heart and animals dying the same way.
entries.question: Which season are you in, and are you fighting it?

entries.topic: No One Can Ransom Another
entries.hook: Wealth cannot purchase one extra day, and the tomb is the permanent address.
entries.question: What are you afraid of losing that you cannot keep anyway?

entries.topic: You Do Not Know What Tomorrow Brings
entries.hook: The sin here is not planning. It is the confidence in the plan.
entries.question: How would you rewrite your plans in James's language?

entries.topic: Where Shall Wisdom Be Found?
entries.hook: Miners tunnel through rock for sapphires. Wisdom is not down there.
entries.question: Where have you been digging for answers that are not there?

entries.topic: Ask for What You Actually Need
entries.hook: A blank cheque from God, and what he does not ask for is the point.
entries.question: What would you ask for, honestly, before you edit the answer?

entries.topic: The Sayings of the Wise
entries.hook: Do not befriend a hot-tempered man, and do not guarantee another man's debt.
entries.question: Whose temper has become your problem?

entries.topic: The Heart Plans, the Lord Directs
entries.hook: All a man's ways seem pure to him, and the Lord weighs the motive.
entries.question: What motive of yours would not survive weighing?

entries.topic: The Vineyard That Yielded Wild Grapes
entries.hook: Everything was done right and the harvest was still bad. Then six woes.
entries.question: Which of the six woes lands closest to home?

entries.topic: Choose Life
entries.hook: The word is not far off in heaven or across the sea. It is in your mouth.
entries.question: What have you made complicated that God calls near?

entries.topic: Moses Dies on the Mountain
entries.hook: He sees the land, does not enter it, and God buries him personally.
entries.question: What might you begin that you will not see finished?

entries.topic: A Wise Woman Ends a Siege
entries.hook: An unnamed woman negotiates from the wall and saves an entire city.
entries.question: Where could one sensible conversation prevent a disaster?

entries.topic: Dead to Sin, Alive to God
entries.hook: Paul answers the obvious objection: if grace covers it, why stop?
entries.question: Where do you use grace as permission?

entries.topic: The War Inside
entries.hook: I do not do the good I want. Who will rescue me?
entries.question: What is the thing you keep doing that you do not want to do?

entries.topic: Living Sacrifices and Ordinary Love
entries.hook: It begins with worship as body and ends with feeding your enemy.
entries.question: Which instruction in the second half is hardest for you?

entries.topic: Firstborn Over All Creation
entries.hook: In him all things hold together, including the parts that feel like they are not.
entries.question: What feels like it is falling apart, and what does this text say about it?

entries.topic: A High Priest Who Can Sympathise
entries.hook: Tempted in every way, and he learned obedience through what he suffered.
entries.question: Does it change anything that he knows how it feels?

entries.topic: Not Because of Works Done in Righteousness
entries.hook: We were also once foolish, disobedient and hateful. Remember that before speaking about others.
entries.question: How does your own past change your tone about others?

entries.topic: Angels Long to Look Into It
entries.hook: Prophets researched their own prophecies and angels lean in to watch.
entries.question: What have you become bored by that heaven finds fascinating?

entries.topic: Make Every Effort to Add to Your Faith
entries.hook: A ladder of qualities, and a warning about spiritual short-sightedness.
entries.question: Which rung are you stuck on?

entries.topic: O Foolish Galatians
entries.hook: Having begun by the Spirit, are you now being perfected by effort?
entries.question: Where have you started earning something you were given?

entries.topic: Come, Everyone Who Thirsts
entries.hook: Why spend money on what is not bread? Buy without money.
entries.question: What are you paying for that God offers free?

entries.topic: A Heart of Flesh
entries.hook: God states plainly that he is doing this for his own name, not because they deserve it.
entries.question: Is that comforting or offensive to you? Say why.

entries.topic: He Will Quiet You by His Love
entries.hook: After two and a half chapters of judgment, God sings.
entries.question: Can you picture God delighting in you? What blocks it?

entries.topic: Their Eyes Were Opened at the Table
entries.hook: He walks seven miles with them explaining Scripture and they only recognise him over bread.
entries.question: Where might he have been walking with you unrecognised?

entries.topic: Do Not Let Anyone Disqualify You
entries.hook: Harsh treatment of the body looks impressive and does nothing for the appetite.
entries.question: What rule are you keeping that is not actually changing you?

entries.topic: The Body That Is Sown
entries.hook: Seed and plant as the analogy for resurrection. Therefore your labour is not in vain.
entries.question: What labour of yours feels wasted right now?

entries.topic: Love in Deed and in Truth
entries.hook: If you have goods and see a brother in need and close your heart, what happened to the love?
entries.question: What need have you seen and closed your heart to?

entries.topic: Do You Want to Be Healed?
entries.hook: Thirty-eight years, and the man's answer is an excuse rather than a yes.
entries.question: What would you have to give up if the thing were fixed?

entries.topic: Do You Love Me? What Is That to You?
entries.hook: Restoration over breakfast, three questions for three denials, and a rebuke for comparing.
entries.question: Whose calling are you comparing yours to?

entries.topic: No More Sea, No More Night
entries.hook: Notice what is absent as much as what is present.
entries.question: Which absence in that list means most to you?

entries.topic: The Lamb Who Was Slain Takes the Scroll
entries.hook: He is announced as a lion and appears as a slaughtered lamb.
entries.question: Where do you expect a lion and get a lamb?

entries.topic: Cornelius and the Sheet Let Down
entries.hook: God has to repeat the vision three times because Peter keeps refusing.
entries.question: What has God said to you three times already?

entries.topic: The Foreigner and the Eunuch Get a Name
entries.hook: The two categories excluded by law are promised something better than sons and daughters.
entries.question: Who does your church make feel like a dry tree?

entries.topic: Love the Sojourner
entries.hook: The reason given is memory: you were foreigners once.
entries.question: When were you the outsider, and who was kind?

entries.topic: Even the Dogs Eat the Crumbs
entries.hook: The only person in the Gospels who wins an argument with Jesus.
entries.question: What do you make of his first answer to her?

entries.topic: Only the Samaritan Came Back
entries.hook: Ten healed, one grateful, and he was the wrong nationality.
entries.question: What have you received and never gone back to thank anyone for?

entries.topic: The Centurion Who Understood Authority
entries.hook: Jesus is amazed by exactly one person's faith and it is an occupying soldier.
entries.question: Whose faith has surprised you from an unexpected place?

entries.topic: Wash Seven Times in the Jordan
entries.hook: A general nearly forfeits his healing because the instruction was too undignified.
entries.question: What simple obedience feels beneath you?

entries.topic: The Woman at the Well at Noon
entries.hook: The longest recorded conversation Jesus has is with a woman avoiding her neighbours.
entries.question: Who avoids the crowd in your community, and why?

entries.topic: The God Who Sees Me
entries.hook: A pregnant slave girl becomes the first person in Scripture to give God a name.
entries.question: Have you ever felt genuinely seen by God? Describe it.

entries.topic: Gleaning in the Field of a Kinsman
entries.hook: Boaz tells his men not to touch her, and quietly instructs them to drop extra grain.
entries.question: What could you arrange so someone can receive without being humiliated?

entries.topic: The Blind Man Who Was Thrown Out
entries.hook: He gains sight and loses his community and his parents' support in one day.
entries.question: What has following Jesus cost you socially?

entries.topic: Go Home and Tell Your Own People
entries.hook: The man begs to follow and is told no. He is sent to the people who knew him at his worst.
entries.question: Who knows your worst and needs to hear from you?

entries.topic: An Alabaster Flask at the Wrong Party
entries.hook: The host's failures are listed only after the woman's extravagance exposes them.
entries.question: What courtesy have you skipped that someone else supplied?

entries.topic: Four Lepers Who Refused to Keep the News
entries.hook: Outcasts find the abandoned camp, eat, hide loot, and then say this is not right.
entries.question: What good news are you sitting on?

entries.topic: Jonathan's Son and the King's Table
entries.hook: One verse explaining how a five-year-old prince became permanently disabled while being carried to safety.
entries.question: What single sentence explains someone's whole life that you never asked about?

entries.topic: Judah and Tamar
entries.hook: A chapter dropped into the middle of the Joseph story, ending with the ancestor of David.
entries.question: Why do you think this is in the Bible at all?

entries.topic: The Donkey That Argued Back
entries.hook: The prophet cannot see the angel. The animal can.
entries.question: What obstacle have you been beating instead of asking about?

entries.topic: Chariots of Fire, Then Breakfast for the Enemy
entries.hook: The blinded raiding party is fed a feast and sent home.
entries.question: What would feeding your enemy look like in practice?

entries.topic: Arrows, and a Corpse That Stood Up
entries.hook: A king stops striking the ground too early and limits his own victory.
entries.question: Where have you stopped short and called it enough?

entries.topic: Jesus I Know, Paul I Recognise
entries.hook: Borrowed authority fails badly, and the city burns its expensive books.
entries.question: What would you have to burn to be free of it?

entries.topic: Rhoda Left Peter at the Gate
entries.hook: The prayer meeting refuses to believe the answer to their prayer is knocking.
entries.question: What answer would you struggle to accept if it arrived today?

entries.topic: Melchizedek and the Tithe Before the Law
entries.hook: A priest-king appears from nowhere, blesses Abram, and vanishes from the narrative.
entries.question: What do you do with parts of Scripture that are not explained?

entries.topic: The River That Gets Deeper
entries.hook: Ankles, knees, waist, then water you cannot stand up in.
entries.question: How deep are you currently standing?

entries.topic: Shepherds Who Feed Themselves
entries.hook: God fires the leadership and says he will search for the sheep himself.
entries.question: Which sheep in your care has wandered without you noticing?

entries.topic: Ebed-Melech and the Rags in the Cistern
entries.hook: A foreign official rescues the prophet and remembers to send down old rags so the ropes do not cut him.
entries.question: What small kindness inside a big rescue could you add?

entries.topic: Everyone Did What Was Right in His Own Eyes
entries.hook: A stolen silver idol, a hired priest, and a whole tribe adopting a private religion.
entries.question: Where has convenience shaped your beliefs?

entries.topic: Bronze Serpent on a Pole
entries.hook: The cure is to look at an image of the thing that is killing you.
entries.question: What are you refusing to look at directly?

entries.topic: Willing Hearts, and an Order to Stop Giving
entries.hook: The only recorded case of a building project telling people to stop donating.
entries.question: What would have to change for your giving to reach that point?

entries.topic: The Goat Sent Into the Wilderness
entries.hook: Two goats: one dies, one walks away carrying the sins into empty country.
entries.question: Which goat means more to you, and why?

entries.topic: Lazarus, Come Out
entries.hook: He delays deliberately, then weeps at the tomb anyway.
entries.question: Why cry over something you are about to undo?

entries.topic: Anointed for Burial
entries.hook: A year's wages poured out in one action, and Judas leaves straight afterwards.
entries.question: What extravagance would you defend, and what would you criticise?

entries.topic: Scoffers and the Patience You Call Delay
entries.hook: The slowness is deliberate and it is mercy, and Peter admits Paul is hard to understand.
entries.question: Who are you glad God has been slow about?

entries.topic: Do Not Even Greet Him
entries.hook: The apostle of love sets a hard limit on hospitality.
entries.question: Where should love have a boundary? How do you know?

entries.topic: The Sun Stood Still
entries.hook: A commander gives an order to the sky in front of his whole army.
entries.question: What have you never dared ask God for out loud?

entries.topic: A Prophet Fed by Ravens and a Widow
entries.hook: God's provision arrives through unclean birds and a starving foreign woman with one meal left.
entries.question: Through whom is God providing for you that you would not have chosen?
